bri.invariant_compare module¶

Backbone Rigid Invariants comparison module.

This module provides functionality for comparing protein structures using their backbone rigid invariants (BRI). It implements efficient nearest neighbor search algorithms to:

  • Compute pairwise distances between BRI descriptors

  • Compare protein sequences when requested

  • Find structurally similar chains based on BRI similarity

The module enables the L-infinity (Chebyshev) and RMSD distance for BRI comparison and Hamming distance for sequence comparison.

bri.invariant_compare.convert_index_table(idx_table: DataFrame, chains: DataFrame, other: DataFrame, keys: list) → DataFrame¶

Convert index table to information table with chain identifiers.

Converts index-based table to a table with actual chain identifiers using vectorized pandas operations.

Parameters:

  • idx_table – DataFrame with columns: distance, idx_1, idx_2

  • chains – DataFrame with chain information (rows indexed by idx_1)

  • other – DataFrame with chain information (rows indexed by idx_2)

  • keys – List of column names to extract from chains and other

Returns:

DataFrame with distance and chain information from both tables. Columns: distance, {key}1 for each key in keys, {key}2 for each key in keys

bri.invariant_compare.group_invariant_compare(x: DataFrame, y: DataFrame | None = None, seq_compare=False)¶

Compare backbone rigid invariants.

This function performs pairwise comparison of BRI descriptors. It uses k-nearest neighbors with the Chebyshev distance metric for structural comparison, and optionally the Hamming distance for sequence comparison.

Parameters:

  • x – DataFrame of BRIs as base with columns: - pdb_id: PDB identifier - model_id: Model number - chain_id: Chain identifier - residue_id: Residue number - residue_label: One-letter amino acid code - x_N to z_C: 9 coordinate columns - chain_length: Number of residues

  • y – DataFrame of BRIs as comparison target. If None, pairwise comparison will be conducted inside x.

  • seq_compare – Whether to also compare sequences (default: False)

Returns:

DataFrame containing pairwise comparison results with columns: - pdb_id1, model_id1, chain_id1: First chain identifiers - pdb_id2, model_id2, chain_id2: Second chain identifiers - L_inf_invariant: BRI distance If seq_compare is True, additional columns: - seq_diff: Number of different residues - seq1, seq2: Sequences being compared Returns None if no comparisons can be made

Raises:

None, returns None for invalid inputs
